payload.name: silicon (diamond cubic)
payload.structure_source: ideal diamond-cubic structure (Fd-3m, 8-atom conventional cell), built with ase.build.bulk; cf. Materials Project mp-149
payload.rationale: Requested by task a819170d: equilibrium lattice constant of diamond-cubic Si from an EOS fit. Well-posed: static 0 K E(V) curve of a perfect crystal is directly accessible with an MLIP; Si is in-domain for MACE-MPA-0 (trained on PBE MPtrj + sAlex).

_fulfilled_need.query: Compute the equilibrium lattice constant of diamond-cubic silicon from an equation-of-state fit.

summary: candidate silicon (diamond cubic) (elemental semiconductor, trust tier)

method.engine: ALCHEMI toolkit environment (mace-torch 0.3.15 ASE calculator, CUDA, float64)
method.protocol: static 0 K E(V) scan of the ideal diamond-cubic cell (isotropic strain, no thermal/zero-point contributions) followed by an equation-of-state fit; 3 strain ranges (+/-2% with 11 points, +/-4% with 11, +/-6% with 15) x 3 cell sizes (8, 64, 216 atoms) x 3 EOS forms (Birch-Murnaghan, Vinet, Murnaghan)

payload.note: Value is the +/-2% strain-window fit (5.4673 A, all 3 EOS forms within 0.0001 A). The mean over all 27 fits is 5.4665 A, range 5.4653-5.4673 A. Wider windows shift a0 down by up to 0.002 A because of EOS-form bias. Cell size has no effect (<1e-5 A). The uncertainty of 0.002 A covers ONLY the numerical/fit spread (EOS form, strain window, cell size). It does NOT cover model error. PREMISE: well-posed. A static EOS gives the 0 K classical lattice constant of a perfect crystal. Si is in the training domain of MACE-MPA-0, which is trained on PBE data (MPtrj+sAlex). So the number targets PBE, not experiment. VALIDATION (same model, same protocol): fcc Cu/Al/Ag give 3.639/4.038/4.162 A. That matches the PBE values 3.642/4.042/4.147 A tabulated in arXiv:2604.07046 (Table C.1, LC20 set) to within -0.1%/-0.1%/+0.4%. The same table gives experimental reference values of 3.595/4.018/4.062 A, so MACE is +1.2%/+0.5%/+2.4% vs experiment, the known PBE overestimate. Also computed, but with no sourced reference on hand: Ge 5.720 A (PBE is known to strongly overestimate Ge), diamond C 3.578 A, B(Si) = 87.6 GPa. COMPARISON: CODATA 2018/2022 Si lattice parameter is 5.431020511(89) A (vacuum, 22.5 C; NIST physics.nist.gov/cuu/pdf/xray_2018.pdf). This result is +0.036 A (+0.66%) above it. That is consistent with the PBE-type bias seen in the validation set. Zero-point and thermal-expansion effects (0 K static vs 295 K) are much smaller than this offset in Si and were not computed. Realistic error vs experiment is therefore about +0.5 to +1% (+0.03 to +0.05 A), dominated by the PBE reference of the model.

summary: silicon (diamond cubic) lattice_constant = 5.467 angstrom via ALCHEMI toolkit environment (mace-torch 0.3.15 ASE calculator, CUDA, float64)/MACE-MPA-0 (medium) static 0 K E(V) scan of the ideal diamond-cubic cell (isotropic strain, no thermal/zero-point contributions) followed by an equation-of-state fit; 3 strain ranges (+/-2% with 11 points, +/-4% with 11, +/-6% with 15) x 3 cell sizes (8, 64, 216 atoms) x 3 EOS forms (Birch-Murnaghan, Vinet, Murnaghan)
